newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Telecom expects to meet 96 budget.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Telecom expects to meet 96 budget.

text.p: Portugal Telecom, which announced a 56 percent profit rise for the first half of 1996, said on Thursday the company was on target to fulfil its budget goals for the year.
The company has budgeted a 1996 profit of 45.5 billion escudos ($296 million), up from 36.25 billion the previous year.
"I see no reason why the company cannot meet the goals laid down in the budget (for 1996)," chairman Francisco Murteira Nabo told Reuters.

Earlier, the company announced a 23 billion escudo profit for the first half of 1996. The result was in line with analysts' estimates although it was over one billion escudos better than the company's own prediction two months ago.

Murteira Nabo, who spoke to Reuters after giving a news conference about the first half numbers, said the outlook for 1997 was very good but that the company needed to get its policy right in three key areas.
The first thing was to fix a pricing policy for 1997 that combined the company's need to be competitive while meeting existing accords on tariffs, he said.
The second task was a restructuring. This operation is to start next month and has been designed to make the state-controlled firm even more market-sensitive, he said.
The third challenge was settling on a global alliance so that the company could compete on an equal footing with other telecommunications operators.
"The entry of the partner will happen in 1997 so the quicker a clear option is made the better," he said.
Nabo said the company would by the end of 1996 assess what kind of a global alliance, and with whom, would be most beneficial.
